'''Claire Voisin''' (born 4 March 1962) is a French mathematician known for her work in [[algebraic geometry]]. She is a member of the [[French Academy of Sciences]] and held the chair of [[algebraic geometry]] at the [[Collège de France]] from 2015 to 2020.

==Work==
She is noted for her work in [[algebraic geometry]] particularly as it pertains to variations of [[Hodge theory#Hodge structures|Hodge structures]] and [[mirror symmetry (string theory)|mirror symmetry]], and has written several books on [[Hodge theory]].  In 2002, Voisin proved that the generalization of the [[Hodge conjecture]] for compact [[Kähler manifolds|Kähler varieties]] is false.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Voisin |first=Claire |date=2002 |title=A counterexample to the Hodge conjecture extended to Kähler varieties |url=https://academic.oup.com/imrn/article-lookup/doi/10.1155/S1073792802111135 |journal=International Mathematics Research Notices |volume=2002 |issue=20 |pages=1057 |doi=10.1155/S1073792802111135 |doi-access=<!-- not free-->|url-access=subscription }}</ref>  The [[Hodge conjecture]] is one of the seven [[Clay Mathematics Institute]] [[Millennium Prize Problems]] which were selected in 2000, each having a prize of one million US dollars.

Voisin won the [[European Mathematical Society|European Mathematical Society Prize ]] in 1992 and the Servant Prize awarded by the Academy of Sciences in 1996.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.math.polytechnique.fr/~voisin/Articlesweb/noticevoisin.pdf|title=Prix Servant décerné par l'Académie des Sciences (1996)}}</ref>  She received the [[Sophie Germain#Sophie Germain Prize|Sophie Germain Prize]] in 2003<ref>[http://www.upmc.fr/fr/recherche/talents_et_decouvertes/prix_et_distinctions/2003/claire_voisin_recoit_le_prix_sophie_germain_2003_de_l_academie_des_sciences.html Claire Voisin awarded the 2003 Sophie Germain Academy of Sciences] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130122040143/http://www.upmc.fr/fr/recherche/talents_et_decouvertes/prix_et_distinctions/2003/claire_voisin_recoit_le_prix_sophie_germain_2003_de_l_academie_des_sciences.html |date=2013-01-22 }}</ref> and the [[Clay Research Award]] in 2008 for her disproof of the [[Kunihiko Kodaira|Kodaira]] conjecture on deformations of compact [[Kähler manifold|Kähler]] [[manifolds]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.claymath.org/news/research-fellow-james-maynard/|title=Research Fellow: James Maynard |work=Clay Mathematics Institute }}</ref> In 2007, she was awarded the [[Ruth Lyttle Satter Prize in Mathematics]] for, in addition to her work on the Kodaira conjecture, solving the generic case of [[Clifford's theorem on special divisors#Green's Conjecture|Green's conjecture]] on the [[syzygy (mathematics)|syzygies]] of the canonical embedding of an algebraic curve.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prizes, Awards, and Honors for Women Mathematicians |url=https://mathwomen.agnesscott.org/women/prizes.htm |access-date=2025-01-16 |website=mathwomen.agnesscott.org}}</ref> This case of Green's conjecture had 
received considerable attention from algebraic geometers for over two decades prior to its resolution by Voisin (the full conjecture for ''arbitrary'' curves is still partially open).

[[File:ClaireVoisinBMC2014.JPG|left|thumb|Voisin at [[Queen Mary University of London]] in 2014]]
She was an invited speaker at the 1994 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Zürich]] in the section 'Algebraic Geometry', and she was also invited as a plenary speaker at the 2010 International Congress of Mathematicians in [[Hyderabad]].<ref>[http://www.icm2010.org.in/ ''International Congress of Mathematicians 2010''] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100208184251/http://www.icm2010.org.in/ |date=2010-02-08 }}</ref>

In 2014, she was elected to the [[Academia Europaea]].<ref>{{citation|publisher=[[Academia Europaea]]|title=Member profile: Claire Voisin|url=http://www.ae-info.org/ae/User/Voisin_Claire|access-date=2015-09-18}}.</ref>  She served on the Mathematical Sciences jury of the [[Infosys Prize]] from 2017 to 2019.

In 2009 she became a member of the [[German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]].<ref>{{cite web |title= Claire Voisin |url=https://www.leopoldina.org/mitgliederverzeichnis/mitglieder/member/Member/show/claire-voisin/|publisher=German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina |access-date=26 May 2021}}</ref> In May 2016, she was elected as a foreign associate of the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/may-3-2016-NAS-Election.html|title=National Academy of Sciences Members and Foreign Associates Elected|department=News from the National Academy of Sciences|publisher=[[National Academy of Sciences]]|date=May 3, 2016|access-date=2016-05-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160506052951/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/may-3-2016-NAS-Election.html|archive-date=May 6, 2016|url-status=dead}}.</ref> Also in 2016, she became the first female mathematician member of the [[Collège de France]] and is the first holder of the Chair of Algebraic Geometry.<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Membres-a-la-une/claire-voisin-nommee-titulaire-de-la-chaire-geometrie-algebrique-du-college-de-france.html|title=Claire Voisin nommée titulaire de la chaire Géométrie algébrique du Collège de France|publisher=Institut de France, Académie des sciences|date=April 27, 2016|access-date=2016-06-10}}.</ref> She received the [[CNRS Gold medal|Gold medal]] of the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] (CNRS) in September 2016. The latter is the highest scientific research award in France.<ref>{{citation|url=http://www2.cnrs.fr/presse/communique/4701.htm|title=La médaille d'or 2016 du CNRS est attribuée à Claire Voisin, mathématicienne|publisher=French National Centre for Scientific Research (CNRS)|date=September 21, 2016|access-date=2016-10-03}}.</ref> In 2017, she received the [[Shaw Prize]] in Mathematical Sciences together with [[János Kollár]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.shawprize.org/en/shaw.php?tmp=5&twoid=79&threeid=264&fourid=501 |title=Shaw Prize 2017 |access-date=2017-05-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170813011758/http://www.shawprize.org/en/shaw.php?tmp=5&twoid=79&threeid=264&fourid=501 |archive-date=2017-08-13 |url-status=dead }}</ref> She was named [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute|MSRI]] Clay Senior Scholar for 2008-2009 and Spring 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|last=MSRI|title=Mathematical Sciences Research Institute|url=http://www.msri.org/|access-date=2021-06-07|website=www.msri.org}}</ref> She was elected [[Fellow of the Royal Society|Foreign Member of the Royal Society]] in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Claire Voisin {{!}} Royal Society|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/claire-voisin-35048/|access-date=2021-07-24|website=royalsociety.org|language=en-gb}}</ref> She was elected International Honorary Member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |title=American Academy of Arts & Sciences Announces New Members Elected in 2022 |url=https://www.amacad.org/news/2022-member-announcement |access-date=2022-05-22 |website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences |date=28 April 2022 |language=en}}</ref> For 2023 she was awarded the [[BBVA Foundation Frontiers of Knowledge Award]] in Basic Sciences (jointly with [[Yakov Eliashberg]]).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.frontiersofknowledgeawards-fbbva.es/|title=Find out about the BBVA Foundation Frontiers of Knowledge Award.|website=Premios Fronteras}}</ref> In 2024 she became the first woman awarded the [[Crafoord Prize]] in Mathematics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.crafoordprize.se/news/this-years-crafoord-laureates-can-see-inside-stars-and-describe-geometric-shapes/|title=This year's Crafoord Laureates can see inside stars and describe geometric shapes -|date=January 30, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/a-mathematician-on-creativity-art-logic-and-language-20240313/|title=A Mathematician On Creativity, Art, Logic and Language|work=Quanta Magazine |date=March 13, 2024}}</ref>

==Personal life==
She is married to the applied mathematician [[Jean-Michel Coron]]. They have five children.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~claire.voisin/Articlesweb/noticevoisin.pdf|title=''Curriculum Vitae''}}</ref>

==Selected publications==
*''Hodge Theory and complex algebraic geometry.'' 2 vols., Cambridge University Press (Cambridge Studies in Advanced Mathematics), 2002, 2003, vol. 1, {{ISBN|0-521-71801-5}}.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Clemens, Herbert|author-link=Herbert Clemens|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/2005-42-04/S0273-0979-05-01056-6/S0273-0979-05-01056-6.pdf|title=Review: ''Hodge theory and complex algebraic geometry I, II'' by Claire Voisin|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.|year=2005|volume=42|issue=4|pages=507–520|doi=10.1090/s0273-0979-05-01056-6|doi-access=free}}</ref>
*''Mirror Symmetry.'' AMS 1999, {{ISBN|0-8218-1947-X}}.
*''Variations of Hodge Structure on Calabi Yau Threefolds.'' Edizioni Scuola Normale Superiore, 2007.
*with Mark Green, [[Jaap Murre|J. Murre]] (eds.) ''Algebraic Cycles and Hodge Theory'', Lecture Notes in Mathematics 1594, Springer Verlag 1994 (CIME Lectures), containing article by Voisin: ''Transcendental methods in the study of algebraic cycles''
